Every Accessibility Workflow. This is a Product Manager case study on a11yOne — a Chrome extension we built to unify automated scanning, manual WCAG logging, project dashboards, and client-ready exports in one workspace. Press enter or click to view image in full size As PM, I owned the problem definition, product scope, build oversight, testing, and Chrome Web Store launch. This article covers the why, what we shipped, how we built it, and what we learned. Executive summary Product: a11yOne — accessibility audit workspace for Chrome Problem: Fragmented audit workflows across multiple tools Solution: One browser-native workspace for scan → log → dashboard → export Users: Accessibility consultants, QA engineers, frontend developers Status: v1.0 built and available in Chrome Web Store Tagline: One Tool. Every Accessibility Workflow. 1. The problem Accessibility audits often fail operationally before they fail technically. Consultants and teams described the same workflow pain: Automated scans in one tool Manual notes in docs or spreadsheets Screenshots stored separately WCAG mapping done inconsistently Client reports assembled at the last minute Enterprise tools help — but many solo consultants and small teams need something simpler, affordable, and workflow-first. Core insight The gap isn’t WCAG knowledge. It’s workflow. Product hypothesis If we unify the audit loop inside Chrome, users can move from first scan to client deliverable without tool sprawl. Working promise: Stop juggling five tools the night before the client call. 2. Product vision & principles Vision One Tool. Every Accessibility Workflow. Mission Make professional accessibility audits as natural as browsing the web — structured, evidence-backed, and deliverable from one workspace. Principles Browser-native Project-first Automated + manual together Local-first trust Deliverable by default Ship the loop first, expand later 3. Target users Primary: Accessibility consultants Secondary: QA engineers, frontend developers, agency leads Job to be done: Organize a client audit, capture findings with evidence, and deliver actionable WCAG-aligned output. 4. What we shipped (v1.0) Create Project — client/project organization Run Automated Scan — axe-core, WCAG 2.1/2.2 profiles Log Manual Issue — WCAG mapping, severity, screenshots, element pick View Dashboard — filters by priority, SC, source Export — PDF, Excel, JIRA CSV WCAG 2.2 Checklist — A / AA / AAA reference Free plan — 5 projects, 5 pages/project Pro waitlist — expanded limits coming later Deferred to roadmap: AI features, cloud sync, CI integrations, billing. 5. Tech stack Platform: Chrome Extension (Manifest V3), JavaScript ES modules, no backend Architecture: Popup + Full App + Service Worker + Content Scripts + Shared modules ComponentTechnology Scan engine axe-core 4.12.1 Excel export SheetJS (xlsx) PDF export Custom MV3-safe writer Storage chrome.storage.local Build Node.js scripts Dev speed Cursor (AI-assisted) Distribution Chrome Web Store Scan flow: User action → site permission → bundled axe injection → normalized issues → project storage → dashboard/export. 6. Key PM decisions DecisionRationale Chrome extension vs web app — Audits are page-context workflows Local-first, no backend — Client data privacy and trust Project-first model — Matches consultant mental model Free tier + waitlist — Lower launch friction Removed risky PDF library — Unblocked Chrome Web Store review Optional host permission — Better security + review outcome 7. Build & launch journey Build: Cursor-accelerated implementation with PM-led scope and QA Testing: End-to-end pass across install → scan → save → export Store review learnings: No third-party libs with remote-code patterns Bundled scripts only (MV3 compliant) Permission model aligned with user-initiated audits PM takeaway: In extension products, compliance and dependencies are part of product delivery. 8. Success metrics Install → first scan Project created Issue saved Export completed Repeat usage Pro waitlist interest 9. Results & next steps Delivered: End-to-end MVP, launch assets, store submission, GTM content Next: Public listing, beta feedback, v1.0.x fixes, Pro packaging Roadmap: AI issue generation, VPAT support, remediation guidance, role-based modules 10. Closing takeaway a11yOne started with a PM question: Why is accessibility audit delivery still so fragmented? We answered with a focused v1.0: one Chrome workspace for scans, manual findings, dashboards, and exports. Not another scanner. A workflow product. a11yOne — One Tool. Every Accessibility Workflow.
